blocks.prompt: 3 (i) Discuss the global extrema of \(f(x) = \sin x + \cos x\) over \([0, 2\pi]\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh global extrema ka sawal hai, closed interval \([0, 2\pi]\) par.
Diya: \(f(x) = \sin x + \cos x\), jo continuous hai. Find: sab se bari aur sab se chhoti value.
Rule: 2.10.3 ka tareeqa: umeedwar sirf andar ke critical points aur end points hain.
Plan: \(f' = 0\) se critical points, chaar values, aur muqabla.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = \sin x + \cos x\), \(x \in [0, 2\pi]\).
Maloom karna: global maximum aur minimum values.
Tareeqa: 2.10.3; closed interval par continuous function ke dono extrema zaroor hote hain.

Critical points
\[f'(x) = \cos x - \sin x = 0\]
\[\tan x = 1\]
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{4},\ \dfrac{5\pi}{4}\]
Kyun: \(\sin x = \cos x\) ko \(\cos x\) se divide kiya (wahan \(\cos x\) zero nahin). \(\tan\) pehle aur teesre quadrant mein positive hai: \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) aur \(\pi + \frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{5\pi}{4}\).

Values
\[f(0) = 0 + 1 = 1\]
\[f\left(\tfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2}\]
\[f\left(\tfrac{5\pi}{4}\right) = -\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} - \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = -\sqrt{2}\]
\[f(2\pi) = 0 + 1 = 1\]
Kyun: critical points aur dono end points, sab umeedwar.
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2}\).

Muqabla
Sab se bari \(\sqrt{2}\), sab se chhoti \(-\sqrt{2}\).
Kyun: tareeqe ka teesra step.

Tasdeeq: \(\sin x + \cos x = \sqrt{2}\sin\left(x + \frac{\pi}{4}\right)\), aur \(\sin\) hamesha \(-1\) aur 1 ke darmiyan hai; yani function hamesha \(-\sqrt{2}\) aur \(\sqrt{2}\) ke darmiyan. Bilkul hamara jawab.
blocks.final_answer: Global maximum value \(\sqrt{2}\), \(x = \frac{\pi}{4}\) par; global minimum value \(-\sqrt{2}\), \(x = \frac{5\pi}{4}\) par.

blocks.prompt: 3 (ii) Discuss the global extrema of \(f(x) = x^{4/3}\) over \([-1, 8]\).
blocks.explanation:
Global extrema ka sawal, fractional power ke saath.
Diya: \(f(x) = x^{4/3}\), interval \([-1, 8]\) par. Cube root negative numbers ka bhi hota hai, is liye function poore interval par continuous hai.
Rule: 2.10.3 ka tareeqa.
Plan: \(f'\) se critical point, teen values, muqabla; aur negative base par power lagane mein ehtiyaat.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = x^{4/3}\), \(x \in [-1, 8]\).
Maloom karna: global maximum aur minimum values.
Tareeqa: 2.10.3.

Critical points
\[f'(x) = \tfrac{4}{3}x^{1/3}\]
\[\tfrac{4}{3}x^{1/3} = 0 \Rightarrow x = 0\]
Kyun: power rule: \(\frac{4}{3} - 1 = \frac{1}{3}\). \(x^{1/3}\) har real \(x\) ke liye exist karta hai, is liye akela critical point \(x = 0\) hai, jo \([-1, 8]\) mein hai.

Values
\[f(-1) = \left((-1)^{1/3}\right)^{4} = (-1)^{4} = 1\]
\[f(0) = 0\]
\[f(8) = \left(8^{1/3}\right)^{4} = 2^{4} = 16\]
Kyun: \(x^{4/3} = \left(x^{1/3}\right)^{4}\): pehle cube root, phir chauthi power.
Dhyan dein: \((-1)^{4/3}\) na \(-1\) hai na undefined; \((-1)^{1/3} = -1\) aur phir \((-1)^{4} = 1\). Calculator yahan aksar error deta hai.

Muqabla
Sab se bari 16, sab se chhoti 0.
Kyun: tareeqe ka teesra step. Ghor kijiye ke left end \(x = -1\) ki value 1 na sab se bari hai na sab se chhoti; is liye woh global jawab mein nahin aati.

Tasdeeq: \(x^{4/3} = \left(x^{1/3}\right)^{4}\) kisi cheez ki chauthi power hai, jo kabhi negative nahin; is liye 0 yaqeenan sab se kam value hai. Aur \([0, 8]\) par \(f' > 0\), yani function barh raha hai, is liye sab se bari value right end par.
blocks.final_answer: Global maximum value \(f(8) = 16\), \(x = 8\) par; global minimum value \(f(0) = 0\), \(x = 0\) par.
